## The Big Picture

Module 1 built your astronomer's toolkit. These diagrams show how everything connects.

---

## The Observable → Model → Inference Framework

This is the course thesis: **astronomers measure a few things directly and infer everything else**.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    subgraph observe["What We Measure"]
        O1[Brightness]
        O2[Position]
        O3[Wavelength]
        O4[Timing]
    end

    subgraph model["Physical Models"]
        M1[Inverse-Square Law]
        M2[Kepler's Laws]
        M3[Blackbody / Wien]
        M4[Spectral Lines]
        M5[Doppler Effect]
        M6[Newton's Gravity]
    end

    subgraph infer["What We Learn"]
        I1[Distances]
        I2[Orbital Properties]
        I3[Temperatures]
        I4[Compositions]
        I5[Velocities]
        I6[Masses]
    end

    O1 --> M1 --> I1
    O2 --> M2 --> I2
    O3 --> M3 --> I3
    O3 --> M4 --> I4
    O3 --> M5 --> I5
    O4 --> M6 --> I6

    style observe fill:#e8f4f8,stroke:#2c5282
    style model fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#92400e
    style infer fill:#d1fae5,stroke:#065f46
```

::: {.callout-note title="Key Insight"}
Notice that **wavelength** appears three times in the observable column. This is why spectroscopy is so powerful — a single spectrum can reveal temperature, composition, AND motion.
:::

## From Kepler to Newton

The L5 → L6 transition is a model for how science works: patterns first, then explanations.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    subgraph kepler["Kepler (L5): What"]
        K1[Law 1: Elliptical Orbits]
        K2[Law 2: Equal Areas]
        K3[Law 3: P² ∝ a³]
    end

    subgraph newton["Newton (L6): Why"]
        N1[Gravity: F = GMm/r²]
        N2[Centripetal Force]
        N3[Mass from Orbits]
    end

    K1 --> N1
    K2 --> N2
    K3 --> N3

    style kepler fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#92400e
    style newton fill:#dbeafe,stroke:#1e40af
```

::: {.callout-important title="The Key Transition"}
Kepler could **predict** where planets would be.
Newton could **explain** why they moved that way — and use that explanation to **measure mass**.
:::

## The Light Lectures (L7-L10)

These four lectures show how much information is encoded in starlight.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TB
    LIGHT[Starlight Arrives]

    subgraph L7["L7: EM Spectrum"]
        EM[What is light?<br/>Wavelength, frequency, energy]
    end

    subgraph L8["L8: Blackbody"]
        BB[Continuous spectrum<br/>Wien's Law → Temperature<br/>Stefan-Boltzmann → Luminosity]
    end

    subgraph L9["L9: Spectral Lines"]
        SL[Absorption/Emission lines<br/>Kirchhoff's Laws<br/>OBAFGKM Classification]
    end

    subgraph L10["L10: Doppler"]
        DOP[Line shifts<br/>Radial velocity<br/>Exoplanet detection]
    end

    LIGHT --> L7
    L7 --> L8
    L7 --> L9
    L9 --> L10

    L8 --> |"Temperature"| TEMP[T from peak λ]
    L8 --> |"Luminosity"| LUM[L from T and R]
    L9 --> |"Composition"| COMP[Elements present]
    L10 --> |"Motion"| MOT[Radial velocity]

    style L7 fill:#e0e7ff,stroke:#3730a3
    style L8 fill:#fef3c7,stroke:#92400e
    style L9 fill:#dcfce7,stroke:#166534
    style L10 fill:#fce7f3,stroke:#9d174d
```

## Summary Table

| Observable | Model/Tool | What It Reveals | Key Lecture |
|------------|-----------|-----------------|-------------|
| Position (angles) | Celestial sphere, parallax | Directions, distances | L3, L7 |
| Position (over time) | Kepler's Laws | Orbital periods, distances | L5 |
| Timing (orbital period) | Newton's gravity | Masses | L6 |
| Brightness | Inverse-square law | Distances (with L known) | L7 |
| Wavelength (peak) | Wien's Law | Temperature | L8 |
| Wavelength (total flux) | Stefan-Boltzmann | Luminosity | L8 |
| Wavelength (lines) | Kirchhoff's Laws | Composition | L9 |
| Wavelength (line shifts) | Doppler effect | Radial velocity | L10 |

## What's Next?

In **Module 2: Stars**, we apply this toolkit to understand:

- How stars are born (gravity + gas clouds)
- Why they shine (nuclear fusion)
- How they evolve (main sequence → giants → endpoints)
- What determines their fate (mass!)

The same Observable → Model → Inference framework continues.
